key_insight: A monolayer graphene front contact improves AlInN/Si solar-cell performance by boosting current collection and efficiency without significantly changing open-circuit voltage.
engineering_relevance: Graphene offers a low-temperature, semitransparent conductive contact that can enhance nitride-based photovoltaic devices while remaining compatible with device integration on Si substrates.
method: AlxIn1−xN solar cells were grown on p-type Si(100) with a thin a-Si buffer layer.
Three Al compositions were tested: x = 0.22, 0.35, and 0.43.
A monolayer graphene film was transferred onto the front surface and compared against devices without graphene.
evidence_signal: Under illuminated and dark characterization, graphene consistently improved short-circuit current density, fill factor, and power conversion efficiency across all compositions, while Voc stayed nearly unchanged.
watch_item: The graphene transfer process and contact uniformity may affect reproducibility and scale-up, so interfacial quality and coverage need careful control.
paper_title: Enhancement of nitride-based solar cells using graphene as transparent contact layer
